title: Lex V2 code hook for the help desk bot
scenario: LFG's Lex V2 help desk bot contained 9% of calls: its code hook delegated every turn, accepted three-digit employee IDs, reset the wrong system on vague answers and handed failures to analysts with no context. Implement the code hook against recorded Lex V2 events so it validates, disambiguates, confirms, fulfills and hands off with a contract the Connect flow and agent workspace can read.
task: Route by intent and invocationSource (DialogCodeHook vs FulfillmentCodeHook)
Normalize and validate EmployeeId with attempt counting; prefill from Connect when verified
Resolve SystemName from resolvedValues and disambiguate multiple matches
ConfirmIntent without reading back IDs; Delegate on Confirmed, re-elicit on Denied
Fulfill reset, unlock and outage; hand off with handoffReason, handoffQueue, intent, slots, summary
Never throw; preserve Connect's session attributes
acceptance: Every response is structurally valid for Lex V2 (ElicitSlot, Close, ConfirmIntent, ElicitIntent rules)
Validation, prefill, resolution and fallback behave per README on voice, DTMF and chat fixtures
Handoff contract complete; incoming attributes preserved; backend errors become handoffs
ANSWER.md explains the Lex config vs code split and how the flow consumes the contract

Week 7 - agent workspace screen pop from handoff attributes
